title: Three Highly Variable Genome Regions of the Four Dengue Virus Serotypes
author: Rodríguez-Aguilar, Martínez-Barnetche, et al.

steps.title: Retrieve DENV sequences
steps.instruction: Download from the Virus Pathogen Database and Analysis Resource (ViPR) a total of 5 885 nucleotide sequences (2 086 DENV‑1, 1 625 DENV‑2, 1 516 DENV‑3, 658 DENV‑4) plus four DENV reference sequences (accessed March 2020).

steps.title: Sliding‑window variability analysis
steps.instruction: Create 45‑nt non‑overlapping windows across the coding‑sequence (CDS) of each serotype and of all serotypes together, align each window with Clustal Omega v1.2.1, then for every window count nucleotide changes and compute synonymous‑/non‑synonymous mutation ratios per codon; record windows with the highest and lowest mutation counts and ratios for later phylogenetic testing.

steps.title: Define genotype datasets
steps.instruction: Determine the genotype of each of the 5 885 sequences, group them by genotype, and remove redundant sequences to avoid over‑representation.

substeps.instruction: For the first dataset, randomly select sequences from different genotypes of each serotype to build six alignments of 30 sequences each (total 180 sequences).

For the second dataset, select the predominant genotype of each serotype in the Americas (genotype V of DENV‑1, Asian‑American genotype of DENV‑2, genotype III of DENV‑3, genotype II of DENV‑4) and similarly build six alignments of 30 sequences each (total 180 sequences).

steps.title: Screen for recombination
steps.instruction: Upload each multiple‑sequence alignment to the GARD (Genetic Algorithm for Recombination Detection) tool on the Datamonkey web server and record any recombination signals.

steps.title: Construct alignments
steps.instruction: For every group, generate a multiple‑sequence alignment using Clustal Omega v1.2.1 based on percent nucleotide identities (p‑distances).

steps.title: Extract variable regions
steps.instruction: From the alignments, extract three 500‑nt highly variable regions (Hi‑E, Hi‑NS2A, Hi‑NS5) and three 500‑nt low‑variability regions (Lo‑NS3, Lo‑NS4B, Lo‑NS5).

steps.title: Create concatenated sequences
steps.instruction: Concatenate the three high‑variability regions into a single Hi‑Concatenated sequence and the three low‑variability regions into a Lo‑Concatenated sequence.

steps.title: Select substitution model
steps.instruction: Run ModelTest 3.5 on each alignment, using the Bayesian Information Criterion (BIC) to choose the best‑fit model; the GTR + G + I model is selected for all alignments.

steps.title: Build phylogenetic trees
steps.instruction: Using MrBayes v3.2 and the GTR + G + I model, construct Bayesian phylogenetic trees for each individual region, each concatenated dataset, and any other alignments required for analysis.
